messages:
support-jen: Hey team — customer #C-982 is seeing intermittent 429s even though their API key shows healthy usage in our dashboard. They say it started after switching to a new proxy provider.
kevin: Can you paste the 429 log lines and the request headers they send? Most NAT/proxy issues are X-Forwarded-For/orig-ip related.
support-jen: Pasted from customer logs (redacted):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-xx" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 52.14.23.9" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Server side log entry: `rate_limit_hit scope=org:acct-444 reason=quota_exhausted ip=34.210.88.12 key=sk-cust-xx`
They claim the IP 34.210.88.12 is the proxy egress NAT, original client IP was 52.14.23.9.
alex: Interesting — our rate limiter stores multiple scoped counters (api_key, project, org, ip). The heuristic should prioritize api_key if present and valid. Is sk-cust-xx active? If not, it falls back to org scope.
support-jen: The customer's dashboard shows the API key active and not over quota. But our logs show key=sk-cust-xx and scope=org. Could be a validation race where key lookup failed and request got credited to org-level counter.
maria: I pulled the auth service trace for that timestamp — there was a transient 500 from key-db (3s). Auth returned a 200 earlier/later but during rate check the key lookup timed out and we defaulted to org attribution. Repro idea: throttle key-db to see fallback.
kevin: Repro steps from my side: run local proxy that strips Authorization to simulate a flaky upstream then send 100 requests fast. Example script:
```
for i in {1..120}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-xx" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 52.14.23.9" \ 
    http://staging-internal.redwood/v1/generate >/dev/null &
done
```
Observation: when auth service timeouts, our limiter counts against org/ip rather than key.
alex: Root cause hypothesis: race where auth lookup and rate-check happen in separate paths; rate-check uses cached token presence flag but falls back to org on cache miss. Need to make the rate-check block on auth result or use a permissive temporary hold.
kevin: Short-term mitigation: enable a per-project higher threshold for org fallback for that customer so they don't get 429s while we fix. I can toggle for acct-444 now.
maria: Long-term fix: change limiter priority order to prefer api_key if Authorization header present and key status fetch in progress — tentatively implement a 200ms wait-for-auth with circuit breaker. Going to open an RFC.
support-jen: Customer ok with temporary toggle if we provide timeline. Can you also suggest a client workaround? They can forward original client IP in X-Forwarded-For and use a dedicated pool of egress IPs to avoid shared-IP bursts.
rate-limit-bot: Created incident INC-2463 for org fallback attribution; assigned to eng-infra and eng-sre.
kevin: I'll push the org-threshold toggle now. ETA for staging patch: 48h. Prod rollout after testing: 5 business days.
support-jen: Thanks — I'll update customer and file repro steps in the ticket with the curl examples.
alex: Also add a regression test that simulates auth-db slow responses and asserts attribution remains to api_key when header present.
